bib.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale

read.skipped: Reference list (offset ~46764 to ~63202 minus appendix start) skimmed only for lineage.

question: Can a single high-capacity, real-time Transformer policy trained on a large, diverse set of real-robot demonstrations perform hundreds of language instructions and generalize to new tasks, distractors and backgrounds?
hypothesis: Open-ended task-agnostic training with a high-capacity architecture that can absorb diverse robot data yields generalization, and data diversity matters more than data quantity.
contributions: RT-1 model: a tokenized, efficient Transformer policy that runs in real time (3 Hz)
A ~130k-episode, 700+ instruction real-robot dataset collected over 17 months with 13 robots
Large-scale evaluation (3000+ real-world trials) against Gato and BC-Z, with ablations of model and data composition
Evidence that RT-1 absorbs simulation and other-robot data and chains into long-horizon SayCan plans

method.summary: RT-1 tokenizes 6 history images with an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B3 conditioned on a Universal Sentence Encoder instruction embedding via identity-initialized FiLM layers, compresses 81 tokens per image to 8 with TokenLearner, and feeds 48 tokens to an 8-layer decoder-only Transformer that outputs 11 action dimensions discretized to 256 bins plus a mode variable. It is trained by behavior cloning on successful teleoperated demonstrations and evaluated on real mobile manipulators in training and two office-kitchen environments.
method.task: language-conditioned robot manipulation by behavior cloning

datasets.name: RT-1 robot demonstrations
datasets.split: 53 instructions held out for unseen-task eval (Appendix I; main text says 21 unseen instructions)
datasets.source: Collected by the authors with VR-remote teleoperation in robot classroom
datasets.preprocessing: All episodes successful (final reward 1); instruction and scene randomization sampled by software module

datasets.name: Simulation pick data
datasets.source: Sim policy bootstrapped from real policy then trained with multi-task RL; used only in Sec IV-C

datasets.name: QT-Opt Kuka bin-picking data
datasets.preprocessing: 4-DOF actions mapped to RT-1 action space (roll, pitch set to 0, yaw kept); binary gripper close made continuous; all relabelled to instruction 'pick anything'

models.name: RT-1
models.tokenizer: images: 6 frames of 300x300 -> 9x9x512 feature map -> 81 tokens -> TokenLearner 8 tokens each; actions: 256 uniform bins per dimension
models.layers: 8 self-attention layers (Transformer); 26 MBConv/FiLM layers in image tokenizer

models.name: Gato (reimplemented)
models.architecture: Transformer, per-patch image tokens, late language fusion, autoregressive actions

models.name: BC-Z
models.architecture: ResNet feedforward, no history, continuous actions

training.objective: standard categorical cross-entropy with causal masking (behavior cloning: negative log-likelihood of actions given images and instruction)

other.film_init: dense layers producing FiLM affine transform initialized to zero so FiLM starts as identity
other.checkpoint_selection: real-to-sim: policies rolled out in simulator over 551 tasks with RetinaGAN image translation to rank checkpoints (Appendix F)

inference.decoding: non-autoregressive action token output (one forward pass per step)
inference.samples: single policy rollout per trial; 3000+ real-world trials total; number of trials per cell not stated except 72 grasping trials for bin-picking eval
inference.prompting: natural-language instruction embedded by Universal Sentence Encoder; SayCan few-shot prompting plans long-horizon tasks

parameters.fixed_wait: 280 ms wait after capturing state before applying action

other.speedups: TokenLearner 2.4x; reusing image tokens across overlapping windows 1.7x

metrics.name: success rate
metrics.definition: Human-rated skill completion; failure if collision, touching irrelevant objects, unsafe behavior, or not done within 100 actions (~33 s)

eval.protocol: Seen: 200+ tasks (744 in Appendix), skill-weighted average; unseen: 21 (main) or 53 (Appendix) held-out instructions; 30 distractor tasks and 22 background tasks (main), 3 and 6 task templates (Appendix); 15 long-horizon SayCan instructions in 2 kitchens; baselines trained on the same data; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported

evidence.quote: Despite its size (35M parameters), it does this at 3 Hz

evidence.where: Sec IV-A; Appendix I says 53 tasks held out

results.setup: Real robot, classroom environment, trained on ~130k episodes, baselines trained on same data
results.quote: RT-1 is able to perform 97% of the more than 200 instructions successfully
results.note: Appendix I says seen eval covers 744 tasks

results.claim: RT-1 solves 76% of unseen instructions, 24 points above the next best baseline.
results.setup: Held-out skill/object combinations whose parts appear in training
results.quote: performing 76% of the never-before-seen instructions, 24% more than the next best baseline

results.claim: RT-1 reaches 83% on distractor tasks and 59% on background tasks.
results.setup: Up to 9 distractors with occlusion; new kitchen and counter textures
results.quote: successfully executing 83% of the distractor robustness tasks and 59% of the background robustness tasks

results.claim: In realistic kitchen scenarios RT-1 scores 70% overall versus 55% for BC-Z XL.
results.table: Table III, row RT-1 (ours), column All

results.claim: Removing 25% of tasks while keeping 97% of data hurts generalization as much as cutting data size by 49%.
results.setup: Data ablation of RT-1; task-diverse vs capped-per-task datasets
results.quote: removing 25% of the tasks while keeping 97% of the data achieves an equivalent generalization performance to reducing the dataset size by as much as 49%

results.claim: Adding simulation data raises real-world success on sim-only objects from 23% to 87% without hurting real objects (92 to 90).
results.setup: 518k sim pick trajectories mixed with real data; real-world evaluation on pick and move-to
results.note: Unseen skills with sim objects 7 to 33

results.claim: Mixing Kuka bin-picking data lifts bin-picking eval from 22% to 39% with a 2-point loss on the classroom eval.
results.setup: 209k Kuka episodes mixed 2:1 with RT-1 data
results.quote: performs at 39% compared to the 22% of the model that was trained only on the RT-1 data

results.claim: In SayCan long-horizon tasks RT-1 reaches 67% execution success in both kitchens; Gato gets 0% and BC-Z 13% in Kitchen2.
results.setup: SayCan planning, 87% planning success for all but original SayCan (73)
results.quote: RT-1 performs the best, with 67% execution success rate in Kitchen1

results.claim: Replacing discretized actions with continuous Gaussian actions drops seen-task success to 68%.
results.setup: Model ablation, MSE loss with multivariate normal output
results.table: Table XIII, row RT-1 w/ continuous actions, column Seen Tasks

results.claim: Removing ImageNet pretraining cuts unseen-task success by 33 points.
results.quote: decreasing the unseen task performance rate by 33%

results.claim: Autoregressive action conditioning did not help and more than doubled inference time (36 ms vs 15 ms).
Model inference budget is under 100 ms for 3 Hz control.
results.setup: Real-robot control requirement derived from 2-4 s human task times

results.claim: TokenLearner and token reuse speed inference by 2.4x and 1.7x.
results.quote: speed up the model inference by 2.4 and 1.7 times, respectively

results.claim: The 1.2B-parameter original Gato takes 1.9 s per on-robot inference, so the baseline was shrunk to 37M.
results.quote: which was 1.2B parameters (resulting in on robot inference time of 1.9s)

results.claim: A fixed 280 ms wait enforces consistent control frequency.
results.setup: Max observed latency of all components
results.quote: (280ms, the max observed latency of all components)

results.claim: Real-to-sim evaluation in a simulator covering 551 tasks ranks real policies directionally and is used for checkpoint selection.

limits: Authors: imitation learning cannot surpass the demonstrators.
Authors: generalization is limited to combinations of previously seen concepts, not new motions.
Authors: evaluation kitchens are similar to training; tasks are not very dexterous.
No optimizer, learning rate, batch size, steps, hardware or seeds are stated, so training is not reproducible from the paper.
No variance, confidence intervals or per-cell trial counts; success rates are single numbers.
Baselines are retrained on the authors' data and shrunk to a similar size; authors note comparison compares architectures, not systems.
Unseen-task count inconsistent: 21 in Sec IV-A, 53 in Appendix I; seen-task count 200+ vs 744.
Dataset and weights not stated as released; code link given.

figures.caption: A high-level overview of RT-1's architecture, dataset, and evaluation.
figures.why: Shows image + instruction -> action tokens at 3 Hz in one picture

figures.caption: The architecture diagram of RT-1. The instruction is transformed into a USE embedding and used to condition a pre-trained EfficientNet via FiLM layers. The resulting vision-language tokens are reduced by the TokenLearner and fed into a decoder-only Transformer, which outputs tokenized actions.
figures.why: Pipeline from observation to tokenized action, mirrors a harness loop

figures.caption: Various data ablations of RT-1 across seen tasks, generalization to unseen tasks, and robustness to distractors and backgrounds. Data diversity has a higher impact on the performance and generalization than data quantity.
figures.why: Diversity beats quantity at a glance
